Summary  
Data source overview: The AI Impacts collection compiles surveys, analyses and public statements that estimate the time until human-level AI. The material discusses systematic biases (selection, publication, group, personal-lifetime), methods used (surveys vs. statements, meta-surveys), empirical findings (surveys give later dates than statements; forecasts remain similar across decades), and proposals for improving forecast accuracy (meta-surveys, calibration on concrete tasks).  
EXTRACTION CONFIDENCE[76] – reasonable confidence that major causal–interventional paths are captured and JSON is syntactically correct, though the highly fragmented source limits certainty.  
Inference strategy justification: The text mostly lists pages; explicit causal chains are sparse. Moderate inference (edge confidence 2) was therefore applied to connect documented biases to proposed bias-correction methods that the same project advocates (e.g. “Metasurvey: predict the predictors”, “Concrete AI tasks bleg”).  
Extraction completeness explanation: All key bias mechanisms, empirical findings and suggested corrective techniques mentioned across the links are represented, giving three end-point interventions.  
Key limitations: 1) No quantitative results are quoted, so validation evidence nodes rely on qualitative summaries. 2) Interventions are early-stage ideas; maturity assessments remain subjective. 3) Section titles are URL slugs due to lack of formal headings.
